# SIGNAL RIDGE: THE SKILLS WORLD
### Design document for the Skills tab of Aditya Shinde's portfolio

> **One line:** Opening the Skills tab drops you into a drivable, dusk-lit mountain world where your skills are not a list, they are places, objects and challenges you drive to and light up, and finishing the ridge turns the whole world from dusk to dawn.

**Status:** v1 design. Numbers marked *(tune)* are starting values, not final. Skill names in the zone table are placeholders to swap for your real ones.

---

## 0. TL;DR

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Where it lives | The **Skills** tab. Click it and you spawn in the world. "Back to desktop" stays visible. |
| First thing you see | The **Skills Notice Board** at the Trailhead, ~12 m ahead of the car. |
| Core loop | Drive → discover a skill zone → complete its small driving verb → the zone's beacon relights → proof (projects) unlocks. |
| Big arc | World starts at **blue-hour dusk**. Each relit beacon pushes the world toward **dawn**. Six beacons = sunrise + final "transmit" moment (Contact). |
| Replay hooks | Night Relay time trial (your "Optional Rally"), daily seed (weather and time), ghost car, hidden field notes, achievements that unlock car skins, photo mode with share card. |
| Look | Stylized-realistic, painterly. RDR2/Witcher-style **lighting, fog and composition**, not photoreal geometry. |
| Stack | Three.js (WebGPU with WebGL2 fallback via TSL) + Rapier raycast vehicle + Blender-authored world + Howler audio. |
| Quality bar | 60 fps desktop, 30+ fps mobile (Low tier), first drive in under ~6 s. |

---

## 1. Vision and pillars

**Why this works as a portfolio USP:** a recruiter remembers *driving through your skills*, not reading them. The world must do three things at once: feel good to drive, look expensive, and communicate your skills in under 60 seconds if someone is in a hurry.

**Five pillars**

1. **Driving feel first.** If the truck is not fun on an empty field, nothing else matters. Handling beats graphics.
2. **The world is the interface.** Skills live in the environment as diegetic objects (boards, lanterns, fossils, beacons), not HTML menus. HTML is only used for readable detail panels.
3. **Art direction over polygon count.** Cheap tricks that read as expensive: low golden light, layered fog, color grading, dust, wet mud, rim light.
4. **Always a goal, never a gate.** There is always something to chase (beacon, field note, time), but a visitor can reach every skill in two clicks.
5. **Respect the visitor's time and device.** Fast load, quality tiers, skip buttons, a plain-list fallback.

---

## 2. Research: what makes bruno-simon.com work

Reviewed the live site and Bruno's own 2026 case study. Summary of what matters for us:

**What it is.** A drivable 3D world where the portfolio *is* the game. The 2025 version rebuilt his 2019 original around Three.js with WebGPU (through TSL, so it also runs on WebGL), Rapier physics, Howler audio, and a world authored in Blender. Source is MIT-licensed on GitHub and the music is CC0.

**What we borrow (ideas and techniques, not assets or layout):**

| His technique | Why it works | Our version |
|---|---|---|
| World authored in **Blender with naming conventions** (object names become physics bodies, Empties become colliders, respawns, area bounds) | World edits don't need code changes | Same pipeline, our own naming spec (section 15) |
| Blender preview matches final output (grass, water, dirt visible while sculpting) | Fast art iteration | Same: vertex-colour/splat preview materials in Blender |
| **Grass as single triangles, ~78k blades, looped around the camera** so ground always looks covered | Huge density for tiny cost | Same trick, camera-following grass field |
| **Instancing** for trees, lanterns, benches, props | Few draw calls | Everything repeated is instanced |
| **Palette texture** (one small colour texture, models sample it through UVs), hidden faces removed, merged geometry | Tiny textures, many colours | Same, one palette for the whole world |
| **KTX2 (ETC1S/UASTC) textures, Draco models** | Small downloads | Same, plus meshopt option |
| Foliage as **camera-facing planes with an SDF leaf texture**; leaves **shrink when in front of the car** | Dense look, never blocks the driver | Same trick on pines and shrubs |
| **Time, weather and seasons** shared by every visitor | World feels alive | Ours is story-driven (dusk→dawn) plus daily weather seed |
| **In-world 3D UI** for projects instead of HTML | Immersion | Notice board, lantern panels, beacon terminals; HTML only for dense text |
| **Achievements → car skins**, some cryptic | Replay and sharing | Same idea (section 13) |
| **Daily circuit with leaderboard** | Concrete goal, reason to return | Night Relay, daily seed |
| **Whispers** (30 short visitor messages, moderated, country flag) | Subtle multiplayer with no physics sync | Optional "Signal Fires" (section 13.6) |
| Spatial audio on every object, rich vehicle sounds | Feels expensive for cheap | Same, bigger emphasis on the vehicle and ambience |
| Quality preset auto-drops on mobile (no DOF, smaller shadow maps) | Runs everywhere | Three tiers (section 16) |
| Controls for keyboard, touch, gamepad; "I'm stuck" respawn button | Nobody gets trapped | Same, plus click-to-drive assist |

**What we deliberately do differently (so it is yours, not a clone):**

- Bruno's world is a bright stylized island. Ours is a **moody, atmospheric ridge** with a narrative arc and a lighting transformation.
- His truck is a toy. Ours is a **heavy off-roader** with suspension travel, inclinometer, low-range crawl and winch-style recovery.
- His content is projects. Ours is **skills made physical**, each with a driving verb.
- We add a **plain-list recruiter fast path** and a **click-to-drive** mouse mode.

**Honest note from the discussion around his site:** some people called it great craft but not a new idea, and said it is slow for pure information. Our answer is the fast path (the Notice Board and an always-available "Quick view" list) plus a genuine narrative arc.

**Licensing:** his code is MIT and music is CC0, so you may study or reuse with attribution where required, but build your own world, models and layout.

**Browser open-world findings worth following** (Cinevva's public "open world in the browser" series):
- Batching instances into fewer meshes mattered more than cutting per-blade polygon count.
- Triplanar projection on cliffs was worth the cost; a **fifth terrain splat layer was not**. Cap at 4.
- Three cascaded shadow maps at 1024 resolution gave acceptable contact shadows within about 2 ms GPU time on their target hardware. Low sun is the worst case for shadow cost, which is relevant because we use low sun.

**Rapier vehicle facts:** the vehicle controller models a single chassis rigid body with wheels as raycasts pushing along spring suspensions. It is a port of Bullet's raycast vehicle, which is the right tool for arcade-realistic off-roaders.

## 3. The world at a glance

**Name:** Signal Ridge. **Hook:** The ridge's beacon network went dark. You are the last driver with a working truck.

**Size:** roughly 700 × 500 m playable area, about 2.5 km of drivable trail. Crossing the longest leg should take 45 to 60 s at cruising speed. Small enough to learn in one session, big enough for vistas.

**Layout principle:** hub-and-spoke with one outer loop (this matches your current map: a central crossroads with five outlying notes).

```
                    THE LAST SIGNAL (beacon ridge, highest point)
                              ▲
                              │  switchbacks, night climb
   THE HIGH PASS ◄────────────┤
   (snow, switchbacks)        │
                         ╔════╧════╗        THE OLD GIANT
   MOTOR WORKS ──────────║TRAILHEAD║───────► (fossil ridge, vista)
   (workshop)            ║ NOTICE  ║
                         ║  BOARD  ║
                         ╚════╤════╝
                              │
              THE ASHEN ◄─────┴────► THE RIVER CROSSING
              SETTLEMENT             (waterfall, bridge, ford)
              (lanterns, village)
```
*Reposition nodes to match your actual road graph. The rule that matters: the Notice Board is the hub, every zone is 15 to 45 s from it, and at least two zones connect to each other without returning to the hub (loops feel better than dead ends).*

**Session shapes**

| Visitor | What they do | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Recruiter in a hurry | Reads the Notice Board, clicks "Quick view" | 20 to 40 s |
| Curious visitor | Visits 2 to 3 zones, takes a photo | 3 to 5 min |
| Completionist | Relights all 6 beacons, finds field notes | 10 to 15 min |
| Replayer | Night Relay time trial, daily seed, ghost chase | Open-ended |

---

## 4. The first meter: Trailhead and the Skills Notice Board

This is the single most important 30 seconds. It must land the concept, teach controls, and show your skills.

### 4.1 Opening sequence (skippable, ≈ 4 s)

1. Fade up from black on a **high wide shot** of the ridge at blue-hour dusk, fog in the valleys, the first beacon tower dark on the far skyline.
2. Camera **swoops down** behind the truck, which idles with headlights on, engine rumble, wind, a distant bird.
3. Camera settles into the normal chase position. Control is handed over. A small line reads: *"Field note: the ridge has gone dark. Start at the board."*
4. **Skip** is always available (Esc or click).

### 4.2 The Notice Board (the "first meter")

A large, weathered timber board under a small shingled roof, with a lantern on each post, set in a clearing with a campfire and supply crates. Dressed with **six pinned cards, one per skill domain**, plus a map pinned in the centre and a hand-lettered header: *"WHAT I CAN DO"* (swap copy).

**States**

| State | Trigger | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | Far away | Cards flutter subtly in wind, lantern glow pulses |
| Approach | Truck within 14 m | Camera eases to a three-quarter view of the board (see 6.4), cards lift slightly, prompt appears: **E / Click to read** |
| Focus | Interact | Camera dollies in. Cards expand into readable panels in a **screen-space HTML overlay** (accessible, selectable text) |
| Card open | Click a card | Shows: domain title, skills (each with a small meter), 1-line proof ("used in Project X"), and two buttons: **Take me there** and **See projects** |
| Take me there | Button | Closes the board, drops a map waypoint, and **lights a trail of lanterns/ground glow** along the road to that zone |
| Quick view | Button on board, always visible | Opens a clean list of every skill, no driving needed |

**Proficiency display.** Do not use fake percentage bars. Use physical metaphors: each skill is a **fuel gauge style meter with 4 ticks** (Learning / Working / Strong / Expert). Honest labels read as more credible than 97%.

**The "Signal" meter.** A hanging brass dial at the top of the board shows **Signal 0/6**. It increases as beacons are relit. This is the progress UI that never leaves the screen (also in the HUD).

**Teach-by-doing.** Place the board so the player must perform one small control action to reach it: a gentle curve (steering), a short upslope (throttle), and a wooden plank bridge over a ditch (precision). No tutorial text needed. A tiny hint row fades in only if the player is idle for 8 s.

## 5. Zones: skills made physical

Each zone has **one driving verb**, **one skill-display metaphor**, **one mood**, and **one reward**. Domain names are placeholders. Replace with your real stack.

| # | Zone | Suggested domain *(swap)* | Driving verb | Skill metaphor | Mood and time cue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Trailhead** | Overview, Signal meter | Gentle intro, steer + plank bridge | Notice Board | Blue-hour, campfire warmth |
| 1 | **The River Crossing** | Front-end / UI | **Ford** the river, cross the narrow bridge | Each **stepping stone / bridge plank** carved with a tool name; drive over, it lights | Cool teal, waterfall mist, spray particles |
| 2 | **The Ashen Settlement** | Back-end / Data | **Slalom** through narrow village roads | **Lanterns** on posts; brightness = proficiency. Drive close to ignite | Warm amber pockets in grey ash, drifting embers |
| 3 | **The Old Giant** | 3D / Creative tech | **Rock-crawl** up the fossil ridge (low range) | Each **fossil rib** is a skill; the rib lights as you pass; vista at the top | Pale stone, long shadows, vast view |
| 4 | **The Last Signal** | AI / Current focus | **Night climb** to the final beacon on the highest ridge | The **beacon terminal** shows what you are building now; also hosts Contact | Wind, flame, sparks, strongest light |
| 5 | **The High Pass** | Tools / DevOps / Workflow | **Switchbacks on snow** (low grip) | **Waypost signs** pointing to each tool, snow-laden | Cold white-blue, fog banks, thin air audio |
| 6 | **Motor Works** | Garage: upgrades and skins | Drive in, interact with workbench | **Workshop wall of tools**, car customisation, achievements board | Cozy interior light, metal and oil sounds |

### 5.1 Beacon relight sequence (the signature moment)

Each zone ends with a beacon tower. When its challenge is done:

1. Short camera pull-back (1.5 s), tower flame **ignites with a bloom pulse** and spark burst.
2. A **light beam or smoke pillar** rises, visible from afar and visible on the map.
3. A single deep horn note plays, pitch rising per beacon (1 to 6), so by the sixth it forms a chord.
4. Fog **recedes slightly** across the world and the sky shifts one step toward dawn (section 11).
5. The zone's **detail panel unlocks**: deeper skill info and linked projects.
6. HUD Signal counter ticks up.

### 5.2 Finale (all six lit)

- The beacons link with **ground-level light lines** along the roads, visible from the Last Signal.
- Sky transitions to **sunrise**. Birdsong replaces wind. Music resolves.
- The Last Signal terminal changes to **"Transmit a message"**, which is your Contact form and links. This ties the story's end to the real call to action.
- Unlocks a **victory lap** (Night Relay becomes Dawn Relay with a golden car skin).

### 5.3 Skip rules

Every zone's panel is reachable from the Notice Board without completing the challenge. Challenges give **progress and style**, not **access**.

## 6. Camera design

Camera work is half of what makes driving feel cinematic. Use a small state machine with smooth, damped transitions. Never snap.

### 6.1 States

| State | When | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Chase (default)** | Driving | Third-person follow with speed-aware distance and FOV |
| **Free look** | Player drags mouse | Orbit around the truck, then auto-recentre |
| **Zone focus** | Near board or terminal | Eased framing of the point of interest |
| **Beacon cinematic** | Beacon ignites | Scripted 1.5 to 3 s shot, control returns after |
| **Map** | M | Top-down overlay (screen UI) |
| **Photo mode** | F | Free-fly camera, depth of field, filters, hide HUD |

### 6.2 Chase camera spec *(tune)*

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Distance behind truck | 7.5 m idle → 9.5 m at boost |
| Height above truck | 3.2 m, plus up to +1.0 m on steep climbs |
| Look-at target | Truck position + velocity vector × 0.35 s, so the camera looks **where you are going**, not at the roof |
| FOV | 55° idle, 62° at cruise, up to 72° on boost |
| Position smoothing | Critically damped, ≈ 0.12 s half-life |
| Rotation smoothing | Slower than position (≈ 0.25 s) so the world appears to swing, not jitter |
| Yaw follow | Behind the truck's heading only while moving forward faster than ~3 m/s **and** no mouse input for 1.5 s |
| Reverse | Yaw follow pauses (no whip-around when backing up) |
| Pitch assist | Blend 30% toward the terrain slope ahead, so climbs feel steep and dips reveal the view |
| Roll | Tiny (≤ 2°) bank into turns; never on the horizon at rest |
| Shake | Small impulse on landings and hard impacts, with a cap and an accessibility toggle |

```ts
// Frame-rate-independent damping (use for position, FOV, yaw)
const damp = (a: number, b: number, lambda: number, dt: number) =>
  a + (b - a) * (1 - Math.exp(-lambda * dt));

// per frame
const ahead = truck.pos.clone().addScaledVector(truck.vel, 0.35);
camTargetPos.copy(desiredBehind(truck, yaw, dist, height));
camPos.x = damp(camPos.x, camTargetPos.x, 8, dt);   // lambda 8 ≈ 0.09 s half-life
camPos.y = damp(camPos.y, camTargetPos.y, 6, dt);
camPos.z = damp(camPos.z, camTargetPos.z, 8, dt);
fov = damp(fov, baseFov + speedT * 17, 3, dt);
camera.lookAt(ahead);
```

### 6.3 Camera collision and visibility

- **Sphere-cast** from the look-at point to the desired camera position against terrain and big props. If hit, pull the camera in along the ray (damped), never pop.
- Never let the camera go below the terrain surface (sample the heightfield under it, keep ≥ 0.6 m above).
- **Foliage fade/shrink** in front of the truck (the SDF-leaf trick) so trees never hide the road.
- Large props between camera and truck dither-fade (screen-door transparency), cheap and clean.

### 6.4 Zone focus framing

Near a point of interest, blend the chase camera toward a **designer-placed camera anchor** (an Empty in Blender with a position and look-at) using a 0 to 1 weight driven by distance. This gives you cinematic compositions at the board, beacons and vistas without scripting each one.

### 6.5 Photo mode

Free-fly camera, FOV slider, depth-of-field, time-of-day nudge, three colour grades, a 3-second timer, and an **export that stamps your name and the Signal Ridge logo** in a corner. Free reach for your portfolio when people post it.

## 7. Input: mouse, keyboard, gamepad, touch

### 7.1 Mouse (full design)

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| **Left-drag** | Orbit the camera around the truck. Release: auto-recentre after 2 s of no drag |
| **Wheel** | Zoom 4 to 14 m (clamped, damped) |
| **Hover** an interactable | Cursor becomes a lantern/hand, object gets a soft **rim outline + small label** |
| **Click** an interactable (board card, terminal, workbench) | Same as pressing E when in range; if out of range, shows a distance hint and offers **"Drive me there"** |
| **Double-click ground** | **Click-to-drive assist**: drops a waypoint flag and the truck steers itself toward it with simple path-follow. Any WASD input cancels. Great for non-gamers and for demo videos |
| **Middle-drag** (optional) | Pan photo-mode camera |
| **Right-click** | Reserved. Do not hijack context menu except in photo mode |

Notes: do **not** use pointer-lock for driving (it traps the cursor and fights the UI). Use pointer-lock only in photo mode if you want a free-look feel.

### 7.2 Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **W / ↑**, **S / ↓** | Throttle / reverse (brake when moving forward) |
| **A / ←**, **D / →** | Steer |
| **Space** | Handbrake (drift initiation). *Not jump.* This is an off-roader |
| **Shift** | Boost (limited meter, see 8.5) |
| **C** | Toggle **low range** (crawl mode) |
| **E / Enter** | Interact |
| **M** | Map |
| **R** (tap) | Flip upright if tilted; **hold 1 s** to respawn at last checkpoint ("I'm stuck") |
| **H** | Horn |
| **L** | Headlights |
| **V** | Cycle camera distance presets |
| **F** | Photo mode |
| **Esc** | Pause menu / skip cinematic |

### 7.3 Gamepad

Left stick steer, RT throttle, LT brake/reverse, A interact, X handbrake, B boost, Y low range, right stick camera, right stick press zoom, Start pause, Select respawn. Rumble on landing, rock hits and boost.

### 7.4 Touch

- **Left thumb:** virtual steering wheel or horizontal slider.
- **Right thumb:** accelerator/brake pedals (up/down zones).
- **Two-finger drag:** camera. **Pinch:** zoom. **Tap interactable:** interact.
- Auto-throttle assist option for very casual visitors. Landscape recommended with a one-line prompt on first load.

## 8. Vehicle and driving mechanics

### 8.1 The vehicle

Your green military-style off-roader: boxy, heavy, a spare tyre on the back, red tail lights. Give it a name in-world, e.g. **"The Ridge Runner"**. Expose on the HUD: speed, gear (L/H), boost meter, and an **inclinometer** (section 9.3).

### 8.2 Physics model

**Raycast vehicle on a single chassis rigid body (Rapier `DynamicRayCastVehicleController`).** Four wheel raycasts, spring-damper suspension, engine force, brake force, steering. Do not use jointed wheel bodies: harder to tune and less stable for arcade-realism.

- Collider: chassis box (plus a slimmer cabin box for believable roll-over), no wheel colliders.
- **Low centre of mass:** shift it ~0.25 m below geometric centre. Biggest single stability lever.
- **Terrain collider:** use a **heightfield collider generated from the same heightmap** as the visual terrain (far cheaper and smoother than a trimesh). Static props use simple box/convex colliders from Blender Empties.
- Fixed physics timestep (1/60 s) with interpolation for rendering, so handling is identical on 60 Hz and 144 Hz screens.

### 8.3 Starting tune *(tune)*

```ts
// Chassis
mass            ≈ 900–1200 (relative; keep consistent with gravity scale)
linearDamping   = 0.05
angularDamping  = 0.8          // stops spin-outs becoming roulette
centerOfMass    = (0, -0.25, 0) relative to chassis centre

// Wheels (apply per wheel; verify method names against your installed Rapier version)
suspensionRestLength = 0.55
maxSuspensionTravel  = 0.45     // long travel = off-road feel
suspensionStiffness  = 28–40    // start low, raise if it bottoms out
suspensionCompression= 2.4      // damping when compressing
suspensionRelaxation = 3.0      // damping when releasing (higher = less bouncy)
maxSuspensionForce   = high enough to avoid hard bottoming
frictionSlip         = 1.6–2.2  // per-surface multiplier applied at runtime (8.4)
sideFrictionStiffness= 1.0
radius               = match visual tyre

// Drive
engineForce          = 2200 (high range), 3600 (low range)  // per axle, 4WD
maxSteer             = 0.55 rad at standstill → 0.22 rad at top speed
brakeForce           = 60
handbrakeRear        = 120 (rear wheels only, reduces side friction)
topSpeed             = ~20 m/s cruise, ~27 m/s boost
```

Tuning method: spawn on a flat test pad, then a 15° ramp, then a rock field. Change **one** number at a time. Record a short clip per change, because feel is hard to remember.

### 8.4 Surface-aware grip

Sample the **same terrain splat map** on the CPU (a low-res copy, e.g. 256 × 256) at each wheel's contact to get the surface type, then set that wheel's friction each physics step.

| Surface | Grip × | Extra behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Packed dirt road | 1.00 | Light dust trail |
| Grass | 0.85 | Subtle drag, grass blades part around wheels |
| Mud | 0.65 | Visible deep tracks, mud spray, drag ×1.4, truck darkens/dirties |
| Gravel / ash | 0.80 | Easier sliding, pebble sound, ash puffs in the Settlement |
| Rock | 1.05 | Loud, bumpy, sparks on scrapes |
| Shallow water (ford) | 0.75 | Splash particles, drag ×1.6, wading sound; depth-limited (no drowning) |
| Snow (High Pass) | 0.55 | Powder spray, long stopping distance, tracks stay |

### 8.5 Driving modes and moves

| Feature | Design |
|---|---|
| **High / Low range (C)** | Low range: more torque, lower top speed (~8 m/s), stronger engine braking. Required feel for the Old Giant rock crawl. High range: normal driving |
| **Handbrake drift (Space)** | Releases rear grip for a controlled slide. Great on gravel and ash, hard on mud. Dust and tyre sound feedback |
| **Boost (Shift)** | Short burst (about 2 s) with a ~6 s refill. Camera FOV kick, engine pitch up, exhaust flame. Prevents trivialising climbs |
| **Auto hill-hold** | Brake held automatically when stopped on a slope with no input, so the truck does not creep back on switchbacks |
| **Engine braking** | Slight drag with throttle released, essential for descending steep trails with control |
| **Steering assist** | Speed-sensitive steering angle (the maxSteer curve above) plus a gentle auto-countersteer on slides for keyboard players |
| **Horn (H)** | Fun, and animals/props react (flush birds near the River Crossing, wake a lantern keeper NPC in the Settlement) |
| **Headlights (L)** | Real spotlight cone with volumetric-looking beam (cheap billboard cone) at dusk/night |

### 8.6 Vehicle feedback (what sells it)

- **Suspension animation** on the visual model driven directly from raycast compression values.
- **Wheel spin and slip** drive tyre sound pitch, dust, and mud spray.
- **Body roll and pitch** come from real physics; add a small cosmetic exaggeration (≤ 15%).
- **Tyre tracks:** write track marks into a ring-buffer render texture blended on the terrain (mud, snow, dust). Tracks fade over ~60 s.
- **Dirt accumulation:** a uniform on the truck material increases while driving through mud/water, and washes off in the river. Visually satisfying and zero gameplay cost.
- **Headlight sway and lantern bounce** from suspension.
- **Engine audio:** pitch from RPM, with layered idle / load / boost loops; separate suspension creak, gravel crunch, water wading, and impact thumps.

## 9. Off-road rules: slopes, angles, recovery

### 9.1 Terrain angle design rules (for the Blender world)

| Terrain type | Slope | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Hub and main roads | 0° to 8° | Fast, readable driving |
| Sustained climbs | 12° to 24° | Hill climb to the Last Signal |
| Switchbacks | 14° to 20° with 8 to 12 m turning flats | High Pass |
| **Rock-crawl sections** | 28° to 35° (max drivable ≈ 38°) in low range only | Old Giant ridge |
| Cliffs, no-go | > 42° | Visually blocked by rock faces (natural barriers, not invisible walls) |
| Side slopes | Keep roll under ~25° on the driving line | Avoid unfair rollovers on the intended path |

**Approach/departure/breakover:** model the truck's visual **approach (front) and departure (rear) angles ≈ 35°** and breakover ≈ 25°. Place rocks and ditch lips on the route so these numbers matter: nose-dive into a gully if you hit it too fast, scrape the rear on a crest.

### 9.2 Stability and flipping

- Anti-roll: apply a small corrective torque proportional to roll rate (≈ 15 to 25% of what it would take to level the truck), enough to prevent coin-flip rollovers, not enough to feel fake.
- **Flip-over recovery:** if the truck is tilted > 100° and slow for 2 s, show a prompt and auto-right on **R**. Hold R for 1 s to respawn at the last checkpoint.
- **Out-of-bounds net:** a soft kill plane under the world and a "back on the road" respawn. Never let a visitor be stuck.

### 9.3 Inclinometer HUD

A small round dual gauge near the speedometer showing **pitch and roll in degrees**, with the sweet-spot arc tinted. It teaches the "off-road angle" idea at a glance, looks authentic, and gives screenshots character. Colours: green under 20°, amber 20° to 30°, red above 30°.

### 9.4 Climb behaviour

- On slopes above ~25°, engine force is automatically biased to the rear axle slightly less and front axle slightly more (simulating 4WD torque split), preventing the wheelie-flip common in raycast vehicles.
- Boost is **disabled in low range** (it breaks the crawl feel and makes rock sections trivial).

---

## 10. World art direction: the "AAA look" recipe

You cannot match RDR2/Witcher 3 asset density in a browser. You **can** match what the eye reads as quality: lighting, atmosphere, composition, and material response.

### 10.1 Art style

**Stylized-realistic, painterly.** Slightly saturated natural palette, simplified shapes, strong silhouettes, real light behaviour. Think: Witcher-style landscapes and RDR2-style dusk, rendered with cheap geometry.

### 10.2 Palette (starting)

| Role | Colours (hex) |
|---|---|
| Sky dusk | `#1c2a44` zenith → `#c46a4a` horizon glow |
| Fog valley | `#6f7f8a` (cool grey-teal) |
| Dirt road | `#4a2e22` wet / `#7a5a3e` dry |
| Grass | `#6b7a2b` olive → `#a29a3a` sun-dried |
| Rock | `#6c6a62` with warm `#8a6f52` highlights |
| Beacon fire | `#ffb347` core, `#ff6a2b` edge |
| Water | `#2f6f6f` with `#9fd6d0` foam |
| Truck | Olive drab `#3d4a3a`, red tail lights |

Rule: **warm light on cool shadows.** Orange key from the low sun, blue skylight fill. That alone does most of the AAA work.

### 10.3 Terrain

- Heightmap terrain sculpted in Blender, exported as mesh + the same heightmap data used for the physics collider.
- **4 splat layers max:** dirt road, grass, rock, and one contextual layer (mud / snow / ash). Blend by painted weights plus **slope and altitude rules** in the shader.
- **Triplanar projection on cliff faces** only, to avoid stretching. Normal maps on all layers, small and tiling with **macro-variation noise** to hide repetition (visible in your current screenshot).
- Road edges get a **soft blend** (worn grass at the shoulders, rut lines, puddles) instead of hard stripes.

### 10.4 Vegetation

- **Grass:** single-triangle blades, ~80k, camera-following looped field with wind. Colour variation by world position noise. Grass parts around the truck.
- **Trees:** pine/birch variants. Trunks as geometry, foliage as camera-facing SDF-leaf cards (shrinks in front of the truck). Distant forests as impostor cards.
- **Rocks and boulders:** instanced from 6 to 8 base meshes with random scale/rotation, moss on top via normal-based shader.
- **Wind** shared uniform drives grass, trees, banners, cards on the notice board, and lantern sway.

### 10.5 Set dressing and environmental storytelling

Props explain the story without text:
- A **burnt-out beacon crew truck** near the Ashen Settlement.
- Hand-painted **direction signs** and warning signs on the High Pass.
- Tents, crates and a radio set at the Trailhead.
- Small **shrines of lanterns** that light when you relight a beacon nearby.
- Old telegraph poles leading toward each beacon (a visual path language).

### 10.6 Atmosphere and effects

| Effect | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Height fog + distance fog** | Exponential fog with colour from the sky; the main "depth" tool |
| **God rays** | Cheap: a few additive billboard light shafts at the key angles, plus screen-space radial blur only on High tier |
| **Dust and mud** | Particle sprites, lit by the sun, kicked by wheels |
| **Embers and ash** | GPU particles in the Settlement and near beacons |
| **Water** | Stylized: depth-tinted, shoreline foam from a painted mask, flow-map ripples, splash particles |
| **Bloom** | Subtle, driven mainly by beacon fires, lanterns and headlights |
| **Grade** | Tone map (ACES or AgX) + a tiny LUT per time-of-day; light vignette |
| **DOF** | Only in photo mode and cinematics (High tier) |

---

## 11. Time, weather and the dusk → dawn arc

| Signal | World state |
|---|---|
| **0/6** | Blue-hour dusk, heavy valley fog, cool tint, dark skyline, wind loud |
| **1 to 2** | Fog thins, first warm pools of light across the ridge |
| **3** | Sky transitions toward deep violet, first stars, beacon lines faintly visible between towers |
| **4 to 5** | Horizon brightens, birds begin, music adds a warm layer |
| **6/6** | **Sunrise.** Golden rim light on everything, fog burns off, final transmit |

**Readability guard:** minimum exposure and a subtle ambient lift at all stages so the road is always legible (the dusk is mood, not a handicap).

**Daily seed (weather):** each day, a hash of the date picks one of: **Clear / Mist / Rain / Storm / Snow flurries**. Weather overlays the dusk-to-dawn arc (rain splashes on the river, lightning at the Last Signal in Storm, snow gathering at High Pass). Everyone sees the same weather that day, which makes shared screenshots comparable.

---

## 12. Audio

Sound is the cheapest way to make a small world feel expensive.

| Layer | Content |
|---|---|
| **Music** | 3 tracks: calm exploration, tension on the night climb, resolution at dawn. Cross-fade by Signal count. (Bruno's CC0 tracks exist, but commission or compose your own for a unique identity.) |
| **Ambience** | Wind (varies with altitude), crickets at dusk, river roar near the crossing (spatial), distant fire crackle, owls/birds at dawn |
| **Vehicle** | Engine (RPM layers), turbo/boost, gravel/mud/water tyre loops, suspension creaks, impacts (surface-specific), horn |
| **Interactions** | Card flips, board creaks, lantern ignition, beacon horn (rising pitch per beacon) |
| **UI** | One soft click with pitch variation; no loud menu bleeps |

Implementation: Howler or raw Web Audio, **spatialised** emitters from Blender Empties, **audio unlock on first interaction**, mute toggle (key **N**, since M is the map) always visible, master volume remembered.

---

## 13. Replayability and features

### 13.1 Night Relay (your "Optional Rally")

A timed run: light all beacons **in order** (or the shortest route you find) starting from the board.
- Clear timer and split times per beacon.
- **Ghost car** of your personal best (record inputs/transform samples at 10 to 20 Hz and interpolate).
- Optional **community ghost** of the top time of the day.

### 13.2 Daily seed

Weather + time-of-day offset + a randomised **bonus route** (e.g., "today the Settlement bridge is out"). Shareable result card: *"Relit the ridge in 3:42, Storm."*

### 13.3 Field notes (collectibles)

Your UI already says **FIELD NOTE**, so lean in: ~24 hidden notes, each a short story or fact about you, your process, a joke, or a tip. Some are cryptic (need a jump, a crawl, a night visit). Found notes are stored in the **Field Journal** at Motor Works.

### 13.4 Achievements → skins and upgrades

| Achievement (examples) | Reward |
|---|---|
| Relight all six | Dawn Gold skin |
| Cross the river without touching the bridge | Mud-splash skin, snorkel prop |
| Climb the Old Giant in low range without a flip | Rock-crawler tyres (visual) |
| Find 12 field notes | Roof lights |
| Finish Night Relay under X | Racing livery |
| Honk at 5 sleeping birds | A secret |
| Find the hidden message about how this was built | Dev skin |

Upgrades are **cosmetic first** (so there is no balance burden). A couple of tiny functional ones (extra headlight range, slightly bigger boost meter) are fine and make Motor Works feel meaningful.

### 13.5 Photo mode and share card

Covered in 6.5. Pre-fill share text with your site link.

### 13.6 Optional social layer: "Signal Fires" (needs a tiny backend)

Visitors can light a small fire with a short message (max ~30 chars) and country flag; keep the max count low (e.g., 30), one per user, **auto-moderated**, and they cannot be placed on the driving line. This follows the Whispers idea but with our own fiction. Skip for v1 if backend time is tight.

### 13.7 Easter eggs

A silent campfire NPC who reacts to the horn; a hidden fossil with your initials at the Old Giant; a "do not press" lever at Motor Works; a cairn only visible at dawn.

## 15. Technical architecture

### 15.1 Stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Rendering | **Three.js**, `WebGPURenderer` with automatic WebGL2 fallback; shaders in **TSL** | One shader codebase for both backends, as Bruno's site does |
| Physics | **Rapier** (WASM), raycast vehicle + heightfield | Maintained, fast, has the vehicle controller |
| Audio | Howler.js or Web Audio | Spatial, simple |
| Build | Vite + TypeScript | Fast iteration |
| Authoring | **Blender** → glTF (Draco or meshopt) + KTX2 textures | Whole world authored in one place |
| State | Small typed store (Zustand-style or custom) | Signal count, notes, settings, best times |
| Persistence | `localStorage` for progress; optional serverless (Cloudflare Workers/Supabase) for leaderboard and daily seed | Keep v1 backend-free |
| UI | HTML/CSS overlay for panels; 3D props for diegetic UI | Accessible text |
| Integration | Lazy-loaded route/module inside your portfolio (only fetched when Skills tab is opened) | Doesn't slow the rest of the site |

*If your site already uses React, React Three Fiber is a fine alternative to plain Three.js. For a physics-heavy game loop with custom render ordering, plain Three.js is easier to keep fast.*

### 15.2 Blender naming spec (adapted from Bruno's approach)

| Name pattern | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `phys_fixed_<name>` | Static physics body (box or convex hull) |
| `phys_trimesh_<name>` | Static triangle mesh (use sparingly) |
| `zone_<name>` (Empty, with scale) | Trigger volume |
| `spawn_<name>` / `respawn_<name>` | Spawn and checkpoint transforms |
| `cam_<name>` (Empty) | Camera anchor for zone focus |
| `emit_<sound>` | Spatial audio emitter |
| `inst_<name>` | Instanced prop source / scatter points |
| `ui_<name>` | Diegetic UI plane (board cards, terminals) |
| `beacon_<n>` | Beacon tower n (1 to 6) with child Empties for flame, light, camera |

A tiny loader walks the glTF scene and turns the names into gameplay. **Changing the world should never need a code change.**

### 15.3 Frame structure

```
fixedUpdate (60 Hz):  input → vehicle forces → physics step → surface/slope queries
update (per frame):   interpolate transforms → camera → zones/triggers → audio params → UI state
render:               scene → post (bloom, grade) → (optional DOF) → HUD
```

### 15.4 Loading strategy

1. **Instant shell:** show a stylised loading screen with the truck silhouette and a progress line, plus the **Quick view list available immediately**.
2. Load in priority: terrain + truck + Trailhead → nearby zones in the background → far zones lazily as the player approaches.
3. Compile shaders during the intro swoop to hide hitches (warm up all materials once).
4. Keep audio loading separate; start music after first user gesture.

## 16. Performance budget and quality tiers

Targets *(set these as acceptance gates)*:

| Metric | Desktop | Low-end / mobile |
|---|---|---|
| Frame rate | 60 fps | 30+ fps stable |
| Draw calls | < 250 | < 150 |
| Visible triangles | < 1.5 M | < 400 k |
| Texture memory | < 256 MB | < 128 MB |
| Time to first drive | < 6 s on a good connection | < 12 s |
| Initial payload before interactive | ≤ 8 MB | ≤ 8 MB |
| Total streamed | ≤ 40 MB | ≤ 25 MB |

| Tier | Shadows | Post | Grass | Extras |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **High** | 3-cascade sun shadows, 1024 to 2048 | Bloom, grade, DOF (photo/cinematic), god-ray pass | ~80k blades | Full particles, reflections on water |
| **Medium** | 2 cascades, 1024 | Bloom, grade | ~50k | Reduced particles |
| **Low / Mobile** | 1 cascade, 512, short range | Grade only, bloom off | ~25k | No DOF, simple water, fewer particles |

**Auto-tiering:** detect GPU class and device type, then **watch the live frame time**; step down a tier if the median frame time is bad for 3 s, and never step back up in the same session (avoids flapping). Expose a manual quality toggle in Options.

**Techniques to keep on the checklist:** instancing for all repeats, frustum culling, merged static geometry, palette texture, KTX2 + Draco/meshopt, looped camera-following grass, impostors for distant trees, baked lighting where possible (AO baked into vertex colour or the palette), shadow-casting only for the truck, large props and the nearest trees, and object pooling for particles.

---

## 17. Accessibility and the recruiter fast path

- **Quick view list** from the very first frame, and from the board at any time.
- **Reduced motion** toggle: less camera shake, no FOV kick, simpler cinematics.
- **Assisted driving** toggle: auto-throttle, stronger steering assist, forgiving collisions.
- **Click-to-drive** for mouse-only users.
- Full **keyboard operability** of all UI; visible focus states; screen-reader text for panels (they're real HTML).
- Colour-blind-safe HUD (don't rely on red/green alone; add shapes).
- Subtitles/captions for any spoken or key audio cues, if used.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-color-scheme` where applicable.
- Pause when the tab is hidden; resume cleanly.

## 18. Roadmap

Build **one vertical slice, polish it hard, then repeat** the pattern.

| Phase | Goal | Deliverables | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0: Foundation (week 1)** | Driving that feels good | Rapier raycast vehicle, heightfield collider, chase camera, tuning flat pad + ramp + rock field | Three friends say "this is fun to drive" without graphics |
| **P1: Trailhead slice (weeks 2 to 3)** | The first 30 seconds | Intro swoop, Notice Board with 6 cards, HTML panels, Quick view, Signal meter, dusk lighting, fog, grass, audio bed | A stranger understands your skills in under a minute |
| **P2: One full zone (week 4)** | Prove the zone template | River Crossing complete: ford, bridge planks, beacon relight cinematic, unlocks, lighting step | Template documented; adding a zone is mostly Blender work |
| **P3: Remaining zones (weeks 5 to 8)** | Content | Ashen Settlement, Old Giant (low range), High Pass (snow), Last Signal (finale + Contact), Motor Works | All six beacons lightable; finale plays |
| **P4: Replay layer (weeks 9 to 10)** | Reasons to return | Night Relay + ghost, daily seed, field notes, achievements + skins, photo mode + share card | Replay loop tested by 5+ people |
| **P5: Polish (weeks 11 to 12)** | AAA feel | Surface effects, tracks, dirt accumulation, full audio pass, tiering + auto-quality, mobile controls, accessibility, bug bash | 60 fps desktop / 30 fps mobile gates met |
| **P6: Launch** | Be seen | Capture a **15-second hero video**, OG image, behind-the-scenes panel, write a short case study, submit to showcases | Public |

If time is short, **cut order**: Signal Fires → community ghost → mobile polish → extra zones (ship 4 zones). **Never cut**: driving feel, the Notice Board, Quick view, lighting, audio.

---

## 19. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Scope creep ("one more zone") | Hard release date; vertical-slice rule; cut list above |
| Driving feels floaty or twitchy | Phase P0 gate; fixed timestep; low centre of mass; angular damping |
| Looks flat / generic | Lighting and fog before geometry; palette discipline; grade early |
| Poor performance on laptops/phones | Budgets as gates; tiering; test on a weak device weekly, not at the end |
| Visitors get stuck or lost | Respawn, auto-flip, waypoint lantern trails, always-on Quick view |
| Cheating on a leaderboard | Treat times as fun, not competitive stakes; rate-limit; sanity-check against minimum possible times; keep it optional |
| WebGPU not available | WebGL2 fallback via TSL; test both every build |
| Recruiters bounce off a "game" | Quick view in the first frame; Notice Board is a clear summary on its own |
